decisions.rationale: A graph permits fanout/multi-input operations without abandoning ordered-layer/track-matte/precomposition semantics. Explicit typed layer operations preserve the normative layer model rather than forcing every arbitrary graph into a simple stack.

canonical_record_rules: Preserve StudioComposition/StudioLayer/property/effect identity and order semantics through typed operations inside the one Folio document. Record output/input port identities and data types, exact time-domain mapping, content references, effect order, masks, transforms, track mattes, adjustments, isolation/collapse and precomposition links.

Layer ordering is semantic input order at the composition blend/stack operation. Layer panel reads that order; graph edits rewire that same canonical input sequence transactionally. A separate authoritative display layer-order list is forbidden.

A graph subnetwork needing non-stack fanout appears in the layer surface as an addressable editable composite/subnetwork row with explicit inputs and diagnostic disclosure; expansion opens the graph. It must not be flattened or hidden to pretend every node graph has a simple stack equivalent.

Existing layer APIs compile to atomic edits of recognized typed layer subgraphs with stable external layer IDs. Layer-only imports use these subgraphs and retain original opaque data/mappings/loss receipts.
A compiled per-frame DAG is a revision-bound disposable projection. It is not the saved authoring graph and cannot become a second writable source of truth.

Materialize stage output addresses for post-mask/post-effect/post-transform/post-matte and retained per-effect output. Fanout references one output with multiple consumers; copying pixels or duplicating layers is not required.

Emit explicit backdrop dependencies for adjustment layers/blend operations, parent-transform dependencies, matte dependencies, effect layer-reference dependencies, 3D-run grouping, quantization boundaries, working/blend-space conversions, source-time/precomp mapping and expression reads.

Source/footage/precomposition sampling and explicit state-provider dependencies are separately time-labelled and budgeted; state/delay providers must declare bounded horizon/recursion/state ownership. They do not relax the property-expression graph law: STU-MOT-077 requires topological property-expression evaluation and rejects any expression dependency cycle at expression commit, naming the participating property paths, including cycles presented as temporal sampling or routed through a delay/state provider. No provider can authorize an expression cycle.

projection_contract.layer_to_graph: A layer insert/duplicate/reorder/effect/matte command patches the typed graph at stable object/property ports, preserving all layer IDs and per-property mappings.
projection_contract.graph_to_layer: Recognized layer-shaped subgraphs produce faithful stack rows; arbitrary subgraphs produce explicit composite rows with input/output inspector. Rows cannot invent a layer order for a graph with no equivalent.
projection_contract.roundtrip: Switching surface or reopening changes no authored records/render semantics/history. Projection caches carry document and projection version/revision and may be discarded.
projection_contract.model_route: Typed commands target the same canonical layer/node/property/port IDs with expected revision/read-write footprints; graph coordinates are optional view metadata.
projection_contract.accessibility: Every row/node/port exposes stable address/type/connection/disabled reason; keyboard connect/disconnect/reorder and inspect-stage commands use same validation as pointer route.
projection_contract.import_fidelity: Layer-native AEP/masks/track mattes/effect order/adjustments/parenting/time/stretch/3D runs remain typed editable graph operations with source mapping; nonmaterialized objects are preserved and disclosed. Binary preservation alone is not editable fidelity.
projection_contract.expression_commit_boundary: Before any expression topology mutation is accepted, Motion validates the complete prospective property-expression dependency graph against current accepted Folio state; STU-MOT-077 cycle refusal remains mandatory. Composite temporal/evaluation planning or state-provider capability cannot bypass, postpone or weaken that commit check.

decisions.selection: Retain current shared control defaults: Shift coarse x10; fine Ctrl on Windows/Linux and Command on macOS via existing Mod mapping; combined coarse+fine x100; Alt has no numeric magnitude meaning. Rebinding changes physical activation of semantic roles only.
decisions.rationale: Candidate SHL106/190 already closes defaults; official Adobe current manual agrees with separate coarse/fine meanings. Combined x100 is Studio-authoritative, not inferred from Adobe or EffectCraft.
decisions.scope: Continuous numeric ScrubValue drag/wheel; gesture routing is contextual, not global shortcut dispatch. Enum/integer behavior needs explicit preserved discrete descriptor rules.
rebind_contract: One Controls gesture-binding configuration maps physical modifier predicates to named roles; per-domain copied maps forbidden. Default Windows/Linux fine maps Ctrl; macOS maps Command through the same native platform adapter as Mod.

Existing keymap parser REQUIRES exactly one non-modifier key, so do not pretend modifier-only gesture roles already work through KeymapSettings::chord_from_str. Extend existing settings/input owner with typed gesture predicates and conflict validation, reusing serialization/platform mapping rather than duplicating keyboard infrastructure.

Operator binding changes validate overlap/ambiguity within the active control context and reserved Alt duplicate/subtract/sample meanings; rejected setting leaves prior map active and exposes a reason. Restore-default and discoverable active hints required.

A modifier-only gesture handler may claim only an already-owned numeric pointer/wheel gesture. Menu/accelerator/graph-selection/pen modifiers retain their own context. Release, focus loss, modal OPENING and wheel inactivity of400ms close the correct actor gesture scope through its normal actor-specific approval route; Escape aborts that scope, restoring its captured pre-press draft value without overwriting another actor accepted mutation.

Accessibility exposes increment/decrement/coarse/fine/reset/type actions as semantic commands and announces effective range/unit/value/step. Operator can type exact values without holding a chord. Model commands address parameter IDs, semantic role or exact value, never synthesize keys.

During active drag sample role each update and accumulate delta in value space; no jump when modifiers change. Freeze the binding-profile version for the gesture; preference changes apply to next gesture, with clear hinting.
One shared descriptor route feeds pointer/key/wheel/AccessKit/model validation and diagnostics/manual/Argus/hintline. Agent gesture state is isolated per author/session and property.

numeric_reconciliation.selected_shared_pointer_sensitivity: Use current canonical SHL191 max(10^-precision, soft_range/200) for continuous pointer drag where terms are declared; omit undeclared terms. Preserve FX110 precision quantum as the discrete arrow/accessibility increment, and store pointer sensitivity separately so pixel travel is not conflated with one key press. Root must amend wording that presently equates them.
numeric_reconciliation.selected_soft_boundary: Retain SHL192 reversible soft-bound resistance for pointer drag as an interaction affordance, never hard rejection; typing exact in-hard-range value bypasses resistance. FX110a free passage must be qualified to mean legal value acceptance, not forced absence of pointer resistance.
numeric_reconciliation.integer_enumeration: Retain FX110 step=coarse_step=fine_step=1 for integer/enumeration discrete controls; do not make modifier scaling skip enum options. Root must explicitly scope SHL190 continuous map or distinguish continuous integer scrubs from discrete selector actions.
numeric_reconciliation.unknown_bounds: SELECTED DESIGN DEFAULT: observed/unknown bounds remain nonconstraints. When no valid DECLARED finite increasing soft range is available, freeze v_anchor at pointer press or first wheel notch; q=10^(-precision) if precision is declared, otherwise q=0; step_default=max(q,max(abs(v_anchor),1)/200), in canonical stored value units per pixel/notch. Fine/coarse/combined roles multiply this resolved step by 0.1/10/100. This is a proposed Studio default chosen from the existing SHL191 magnitude-relative requirement, not a claim that an upstream implements it.
numeric_reconciliation.arithmetic_note: SHL191 statement that max formula always makes 200px traverse the soft range exactly once is false when precision quantum exceeds soft_range/200. Preserve max formula, amend claim to at-most-200px traversal in that case with quantization; fixture required.

Separate pointer sensitivity from discrete input quantum and correct exactly-200px assertion; avoid double multiplying resolved ParamSpec.coarse/fine plus modifier factors.
Separate value legality from pointer-only reversible soft resistance and preserve typed entry rejection outside hard bounds.

unknown_bound_fallback.trigger: Continuous numeric value with no usable declared soft range; missing one endpoint, unknown/observed-only provenance, nonfinite or nonincreasing endpoints cannot manufacture a usable range. A valid declared soft range keeps SHL191 range-based sensitivity even when hard bounds are unknown.
unknown_bound_fallback.formula: q = precision declared ? 10^(-precision) : 0; magnitude = max(abs(v_anchor), 1); step_default = max(q, magnitude/200); step_fine=step_default/10; step_coarse=step_default*10; step_combined=step_default*100
unknown_bound_fallback.unit: One canonical stored value unit is the explicit minimum reference magnitude. Display percentage/unit conversion never changes the stored-domain step; the same profile/unit descriptor renders operator, accessible and model values.
unknown_bound_fallback.anchor_lifetime: Capture finite current value and descriptor/binding revision on press or first wheel notch, using SHL194 coalescing scope. Retain anchor and step through continuous role changes and wheel bursts; reset only for the next gesture after release, focus loss, modal OPENING, Escape or400ms after the last wheel notch. Never recompute magnitude from intermediate values, avoiding feedback acceleration and zero-crossing jumps.
unknown_bound_fallback.accumulation: Apply per-event signed travel to current accumulator with the effective role factor; keep fractions in value space. Clamp only declared hard bounds under current provenance; reject nonrepresentable/nonfinite arithmetic with structured diagnostic without inventing a bound. Unknown bounds do not imply legal NaN/infinity.
unknown_bound_fallback.discrete_exception: FX110 integer/enumeration discrete actions retain exactly-one-domain-step behavior and are not forced through floating magnitude fallback. Numeric precision is a resolution signal, not an inferred minimum/maximum.
rationale: Reuses canonical SHL191 divisor200 rather than inventing a second sensitivity scale.
Absolute magnitude treats positive/negative values symmetrically; reference1 keeps zero and tiny values controllable with fine role.
Freezing the anchor at the existing SHL194 gesture boundary prevents nonlinear acceleration and modifier-induced jumps.
Canonical stored units avoid percent-display x100 double scaling; all routes expose the same resolved sensitivity.
Precision floor respects declared resolution; no precision, range, hard-bound or default metadata is invented.
proof_requirements: Zero, negative, near-zero, very-large finite and precision-dominant anchors produce exact resolved metadata before interaction.
Changing intermediate value through zero does not recalculate sensitivity; modifier changes affect subsequent delta only.
A wheel burst shares one step until400ms idle; next gesture takes a fresh current-value anchor.
Unknown/observed endpoints introduce neither clamp nor fake soft resistance; declared endpoints retain their actual semantics.
Stored0..1 percent display uses stored-domain fallback and displays converted step consistently; no secondx100 factor.
Independent model/AccessKit/pointer routes read the same resolved descriptor and target identity; numeric overflow reports an explicit rejected operation.

Every exact SHL194 exit produces one history-scope entry: release, focus loss, modal OPENING and400ms_after_last_wheel_notch finalize through actor-specific approval; Escape records one aborted scope entry, restores draft pre-press value under conflict safeguards, produces no accepted document-content mutation and stays excluded from undo/redo cursor.

gesture_exit_contract.scope_open: Pointer press or first wheel notch opens one coalescing scope keyed by author_id; intermediate proposed values remain in that actor scope.
gesture_exit_contract.finalizing_route: Each valid finalizing exit closes into exactly one gesture history-scope entry and finalizes through the actor-specific normal approval/promotion route; no exit bypasses grants, read/write preconditions or model approval. Modal closing is not the trigger. Conflicts keep explicit rejected/conflicted disposition without overwriting current accepted content.

escape.draft_value: Restore captured pre-press value in the actor proposal/draft scope under conflict safeguards.
escape.rule: Exactly one aborted history-scope entry is recorded for observability. It is excluded from the document undo/redo cursor; zero entries or an additional rollback content edit would violate selected exit semantics.

gesture_exit_contract.independent_proof: Drive each of the five exits separately, fresh scope each; independently reread history scope count/disposition and accepted document value/EventLedger plus undo/redo cursor. Scope entry count and document content transaction count are separate observations; fixture must not conflate them.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: Agents A and B edit color on node X and radius on node Y with independent read/write footprints.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: Both admitted when current target versions/read dependencies still hold; do not whole-document-CAS reject B solely because A committed. Re-evaluate dependent outputs, not all unrelated frames.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: A connects X -> Y while B connects Y -> X; each patch was acyclic on its base.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: CRDT draft may contain proposed conflicting edges; serialized promotion validates candidate against current accepted graph. Second transaction is rejected/conflicted with exact cycle path; never accept cycle or silently delete arbitrary edge.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: A rewires same target input as B; or deletes a node B reads/references.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: Single input port is one register mutation with expected target version; conflicting reassignment/deletion needs explicit proposal resolution. No timestamp-last-wins promotion of an unintended source.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: A reorders layer above adjustment while B edits that adjustment strength expecting old backdrop.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: Reorder writes composition input sequence and invalidates backdrop-read dependency stamps. B rechecks its intended read-set; stale semantic snapshot cannot be promoted as independent merely because scalar property differs.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: A inspects shared intermediate while B updates upstream and renderer finishes old revision.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: Actor-local stage viewers keep explicit stale revision; obsolete render cannot publish as current. Cache keys bind graph/node/port/time/color/profile/provider/version/ROI/upstream content digest; budgets span fanout result retention.

crdt_and_commit_conflicts.scenario: Lost reply after accepted topology edit or undo during another actor mutation.
crdt_and_commit_conflicts.decision: Idempotency key resolves committed receipt on retry. Chronicle inverse operation checks expected property/topology state and actor scope; it cannot roll back another actor edit wholesale.
